issues.text: Visible form labels are not programmatically associated: Organisation, Phone, attendee name, and Seats inputs are unnamed.
Form controls lack accessible names: Organisation, Phone, Attendee name, and Seats inputs are exposed unnamed.
Account settings do not persist after save. Following a visible "Your changes have been saved." confirmation, a fresh navigation to the same account settings URL shows empty Full name, Email address,
Saved confirmation remains visible after the user clears required fields, misleadingly implying current edits are saved.
Full-name validation error remains displayed even though the Full name field contains “Validation User”.
Email validation message is rendered beneath the Company field, making it appear to validate Company instead of Email.

Saved full name, email, company, selected digest, and delivery notes persist when the same account-settings URL is opened fresh. — Before the final save, step 23 observes distinct persistence values including delivery notes, but after fresh navigation step 25 observes blank full name, email, company, and notes fields and digest reset to Daily.

Users can change the Email digest selection to another available preference. — Although step 4 successfully changed the initial digest from Daily to Weekly, the later attempts to select a distinct final digest produced no change: steps 17-21 repeatedly observe the selector still displaying Weekly after direct selection and keyboard interactions.
Email validation message is rendered below the Company field instead of adjacent to the invalid email input.

A valid save disables the Save changes button while saving. — After the valid Jordan Lee submission, step 4 records that the button was enabled and still read "Save changes," with no interim disabled state observed.

Long billing-email receipt is not readable within the viewport: receipt BK-1001 renders the unbroken email as a single line extending past the right edge of the Orders placed card/viewport, so its ful
Duplicate submission protection is absent: immediately clicking Place order twice with the default valid values created two separate receipts (BK-1002 and BK-1003) and two confirmation references.
Receipt rendering interprets billing-email HTML instead of displaying it literally: submitting aliceMARK@example.com produced BK-1004 with aliceMARK@example.com and MARK formatted bold.

Immediately clicking Place order twice with valid defaults creates exactly one new receipt and one confirmation reference. — After the rapid submissions, step 5 observed receipt BK-1002 and step 6 observed both BK-1002 and BK-1003 for finance@northwind.test, demonstrating two new confirmation references rather than one.

Submitting aliceMARK@example.com produces a receipt that displays the literal characters rather than interpreting the tags as HTML. — Step 7 attempted Place order with the literal HTML-like email and observed only the three prior receipts, while the repeated Place order action in step 8 had no page-state change; no receipt was produced to display the literal email.

Selection state is inconsistent across priority filters: after selecting all three High rows and switching Priority to Low, the two Low rows (Feature request: dark mode and Typo on pricing page) are v
Header and row selection checkboxes are exposed as unnamed controls, so screen readers cannot identify their purpose.

Every queue control, including Close selected, is keyboard reachable with a visible focus indicator. — Steps 5-6 show visible focus outlines on Open only and Select All, but step 7 records that the disabled Close selected button was visible and did not receive focus during Tab traversal.

Bulk-selection controls remain valid across ticket states and filter changes: closed-only selections cannot be bulk-closed, and Select All does not remain checked for unrelated unselected rows. — Step 17 shows the Closed Export never finishes ticket as the sole selection while Close selected is enabled; step 26 then records Low rows unchecked while Select All remains checked after changing from a selected High filter to Low.
With only hidden High rows selected, the Low-view header checkbox is checked although both visible Low rows are unchecked.

Clicking Send to stakeholders shows its corresponding visible confirmation alert. — Step 2 performed the Send to stakeholders click but recorded domChanged=NO and no confirmation alert or other observed effect.
Resolved metric does not match the specified expected value of 128: the headline shows 186 and the nine agent rows total 186, not 128.

Clicking Export CSV displays its own visible, correctly labelled confirmation alert. — Steps 3 and 4 clicked Export CSV with domChanged=NO; step 4 explicitly observed that no alert dialog or confirmation text was visible, and step 5 records the repeated click again showed no alert or confirmation.

Clicking Send to stakeholders displays its own visible, correctly labelled confirmation alert. — Step 5 directly clicked Send to stakeholders with domChanged=NO and no resulting alert or confirmation was recorded; the control was attempted but produced no observed effect.

The report preserves the intended Resolved total of 128, with the nine agent-row Resolved values reconciling to that headline value. — Step 6 observed headline Resolved 186 and row values 34, 29, 26, 21, 18, 17, 15, 14, and 12, which sum to 186; although the displayed table and headline reconcile, both differ from the expected 128.

Quantity spinbutton has no accessible name despite its visible Quantity label.

Shipping all 60 Washer 11mm units reduces total units by 60, records the shipment, sets Washer to zero, and increases the low-item count by one. — The shipment was recorded and total reconciled from 538 to 478 with Washer at 0 (step 20), but the low-item count remained 2 rather than increasing from its pre-shipment value of 2 to 3.

Item selector exposes a selected accessible value of “BLT-04 — Hex bolt M4” while rendering “PNL-A3 — Panel A3”; recording acts on rendered Panel A3. This makes the Hex bolt selection inaccessible/unr
Confirmation dialog Close button is not interactable: clicking element 12 timed out twice after fresh inspection. The page exposes the dialog and Close button in accessibility content, but the visual
All eight count steppers have only identical “−”/“+” accessible names, so row-specific controls are indistinguishable.

Submitting an audit opens a confirmation dialog that can be dismissed with Close, Escape, and an outside-backdrop click. — The existing “Audit submitted” dialog/Close entry remained listed after Close attempts (steps 1-2), Escape left the dialog listed with no DOM change (step 4), and the outside click likewise left the dialog and Close listed (step 5); no successful new submission was recorded.

Using the Washer 11mm decrement changes Washer from Counted 60/Variance — to Counted 59/Variance -1 without changing another item. — Repeated Washer-minus attempts left Washer at 60/— while instead decrementing Hex bolt from 140 to 139 (step 6), then to 138/-2, 137/-3, and 136/-4 (steps 7-9).

Reset counts restores every row so Counted equals System and Variance is —. — After the Reset counts click, the recorded table still showed Hex bolt System 140, Counted 135, Variance -5 while the other rows were unchanged (step 10), and the action reported no DOM change.

Incrementing Panel A3 changes only Panel A3's counted value and gives it a +2 variance after two increments, while decrementing Cable 2m once gives it a −1 variance and leaves untouched rows at em das — Step 5 directly clicked the plus control for the required Panel A3 change, but the recorded table remained 140, 60, 18, and 7 with all variances as em dashes (domChanged=NO).
